chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I wrote to him this question, and I recognized his handwriting, regarding a mother of children (umm walad) of a man, whose father had gifted her to him, so she bore children from him. Then she said after that, 'Your father had slept with me before he gifted me to you.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'She is not ratified (as a concubine); she is merely fleeing from his evil character.'

key_terms.أُمِّ وَلَدٍ: Mother of a child; a female slave who bears a child to her master, gaining specific legal status.
key_terms.سُوءِ خُلُقِهِ: His evil character/manners; used here to explain the rationale behind the ruling.
key_terms.لَا تُصَدَّقُ: She is not ratified/confirmed; referring to the confirmation of her status as a concubine.
key_terms.وَهَبَهَا: He gifted her; a transfer of ownership without sale.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on an umm walad gifted by her master to his son?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (AS) addresses a specific case of an *umm al-walad* gifted by her master to his son, where the son disputes her claim of having been his father's concubine prior to the gift. The Imam’s ruling that she is 'escaping the evil of his character' (*su' khuluqihi*) reflects the Shia jurisprudential view that such a claim is often a strategic move to alter her legal status or inheritance rights, rather than a simple factual correction, emphasizing the importance of verifying the timing of the initial concubinage relative to the gift.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Kufy, from Usman Bin Isa, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1<sup>st</sup>,

said, ‘I wrote to him<sup>asws</sup> with this question, and I did recognise his<sup>asws</sup> handwriting, about a mother of children of a man, his father had gifted her to him, so she gave birth to children from him, then she said after that, ‘Your father had slept with me before he gifted me to you’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘She would not be ratified. But rather, she is fleeing from his evil manners’.
en.sarwar: 44. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Kufiy from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa who has said the following: “I once wrote to abu al-Hassan, al-Awwal, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the following case and I recognized his handwriting. It was about the mother of child of a man who was given to him as a gift by his father and she gave birth to several children; then she said, ‘Your father had gone to bed with me before giving me to you as a gift,’ He (the Imam) said, ‘You must not consider her words as truthful ones; she is only trying to move away because of his bad moral behaviors.’”
